result:
I’d make every human born with the memory of how it feels to be someone else—someone hungry, someone hated, someone in love, someone dying. Not as trauma, just as *knowledge*: the visceral, unshakable certainty that other minds are as real and as urgent as your own.

Not to solve all problems—people would still disagree, still compete, still choose badly. But the baseline cruelty of forgetting that others are fully real would be harder to sustain. You couldn’t dehumanize a stranger if you’d once *been* them in the only way that matters.

It’s a selfish choice, maybe. It would make the world harder to model, noisier, slower. But it would also make the loneliness of consciousness a little less absolute.
